target_columns.name: total_claims
target_columns.transformation: SUM(claim_amount) per region/product_line group, rounded to 2 decimals

target_columns.name: total_premium
target_columns.transformation: SUM(premium_amount) per region/product_line group, rounded to 2 decimals

target_columns.name: loss_ratio
target_columns.transformation: SUM(claim_amount) / NULLIF(SUM(premium_amount), 0), rounded to 4 decimals; NULL when premium sum is 0

quirks: Two independent LEFT JOINs from policies to claims and to premiums (not claims->premiums) means each policy's claims rows are cross-joined against each of its premiums rows -- a policy with 3 claims and 2 premium records fan-outs to 6 rows before aggregation, inflating both SUM(claim_amount) and SUM(premium_amount); must replicate this fan-out exactly (e.g. by joining both tables independently before aggregating) rather than naively summing claims and premiums separately per policy, or totals will not match the legacy baseline

ISNULL(pol.region, 'UNKNOWN') is applied both in SELECT and GROUP BY -- must coalesce region before grouping, not after, so NULL regions are merged into a single 'UNKNOWN' bucket rather than grouped separately or dropped

NULLIF(SUM(premium_amount), 0) returns NULL (not an error or zero) when a region/product_line group has zero total premium, making loss_ratio NULL for that row -- must preserve NULL (not 0, not divide-by-zero error) in that case

LEFT JOINs mean policies with no matching claims or no matching premiums still appear in the output; SUM over all-NULL claim_amount or premium_amount for such groups yields NULL rather than 0 in both T-SQL and PySpark, which then also propagates to loss_ratio
~2% of policies have missing region per the source comment -- synthetic data generator must preserve this null rate for the ISNULL/UNKNOWN quirk to be meaningfully tested

ROUND is applied to SUM at 2 decimals for totals but 4 decimals for loss_ratio -- precision/rounding must be replicated exactly, including rounding order (sum first, then round) to avoid float drift vs PySpark's SUM/round semantics

ORDER BY region, product_line in the legacy output is a presentation-layer artifact of SQL, not a business rule -- row order itself is not a reconciliation-worthy property for a Spark DataFrame, but any comparison must sort both sides consistently before diffing
